$ go test  # ladder-a
    the column parse is owned by . and ./b. Column names are unique per corpus root, and one package owns each column.
        Rename one of the columns, or remove one. A package that only reads a lift's product gives the lift to hypercase.Use.
    what ran, in order:
        parse ran on x
        resolve ran on x
        evaluate's probe ran
        evaluate ran on x

            --- PASS: TestCorpus/script/x/parse
            --- PASS: TestCorpus/script/x/resolve
FAIL
[exit 1]
$ rm b/corpus_test.go  # remove b's tests, and leave its registry
$ go test  # ladder-a

        Delete it, or restore the package's tests.

$ go test  # ladder-a-useonly
    b/testdata/hypercase.json is a registry, and b holds no _test.go file, so no test compares it, and it still claims sections.
        Delete it, or restore the package's tests.
    the lift parse is used by ., and no package owns it, so its error is recorded nowhere. The registry of ./b records that its package owns the lift, and ./b holds no _test.go file, so no test runs the lift there.
        Restore the tests of ./b, or delete its registry and own the lift in one of the packages that use it: give it to hypercase.Own in place of hypercase.Use.
